rationale: Equally supported explicit search filters in an authored semantic list should follow that source list, rather than promoting a shorter label and displacing a source peer from the first six cards. This is an explicit first-screen tie-policy change using generic structural evidence, not an evaluation-label rule.

policy.eligible: category search, pageTask control, supplementalDependent, and current supplementalEvidence.filter; nearest semantic ul/ol/role=list and same actual form owner are required
policy.ordering: Sort by existing comparator first; replace only each tied form/list group's existing positions using source DOM order. Separate groups never borrow positions. The existing reading-group policy is preserved.
policy.cache: One fresh SupplementalCache within each ordered() pass; no retained rank or currentness cache. Filter metadata checks are local; no whole-form scan or input values are read.
policy.complexity: Push group indices, then sort tied groups; no additional per-candidate whole-form scans or growing filter-array copies.

baseline.note: The separate initial-one-character-fixture.log contains invalid one-character synthetic labels rejected by the existing classifier. Those labels were corrected to safe unknown two-character terms before the meaningful baseline above. No source patch preceded that meaningful baseline.

final.command: npx playwright test tests/filter-ordering.spec.mjs tests/ranker-capacity.spec.mjs tests/classifier-ranking.spec.mjs

coverage: unknown synthetic filter names preserve DOM order despite differing label lengths
different scores or purposes retain existing precedence
separate lists within one form keep existing group positions
separate forms and global search input do not mix
first six and overflow retain source order and offer each original once
ordinary search menus without explicit filter evidence retain lexical/length policy
a later ordering batch sees changed form metadata and does not reuse old evidence

boundary.notes: Only routed/blocked headless local synthetic fixtures. Parent owns full integration, development metrics, source freeze, documentation and acceptance. Other source owners worked concurrently, so this report does not claim a global source freeze.
